messages.subject: Re: Questions about Bridging Registrations
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tatsuo,

Thanks for your message. I'm glad these resources are proving useful to
you. Please see inline for responses to your queries. note that I have
cced the nat-user group in reply so that others may benefit from this
information.

On 11 Aug 2016, at 22:38, Tatsuo Okubo wrote:

> I hope this e-mail finds you well.
> I am a post-doc in Rachel Wilson's lab, and I had a quick question
> about
> your Bridging Registration tool that I found to be extremely useful.
>
> (1) Visualizing FlyCircuit neurons in BrainGazer
> Do you have recommendations on how to transform FlyCircuit images so
> that
> they can be viewed in BrainGazer?
>
> When I tried the following, the output image only contained the right
> half
> of the neuron.
>
> cmtk reformatx --floating sample_image.nrrd T1.nrrd T1_FCWB.list

Where does this sample_image.nrrd come from? Is it registered in FCWB
space? The starting image must already be registered to use this
approach. It must also be spatially calibrated to match the FCWB voxel
dimensions.

I have not used BrainGazer for some years. Does it now support nrrd as
well as amiramesh input files? If it supports swc files, then you may
prefer to use skeletonised neurons for visualisation rather than image
volumes. This would be more efficient, allowing a greater number of
neurons to be visualised simultaneously. Our R tools would enable you to
bridge registered neuron skeletons to the T1 (BrainGazer) space and then
write them out in swc format.

You might also like to consider Vaa3d or fluorender as visualisation
alternatives that do include support for nrrd and swc formats.

> (2) Images of Janelia GAL4 lines.
> I found the reformatted data of Janelia FlyLight lines (~3500) to be
> also
> very useful.
> http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/vfb/jfrc/fl/reformatted-quant/
> Currently, there seems to be 4000 lines available through Bloomington,
> and
> I was wondering if there are any plans on having additional images for
> the
> remaining 500 lines in the future.

Gerry Rubin and co-authors distributed 3501 unregistered brain Gal4
images when they published the Jenett 2012 paper. This is what we then
registered and have made available at that link. At this point about
2500 of those lines are available from Bloomington. The additional 1500
Bloomington lines should represent lines for which no image data has
been published.

Best wishes,

Greg.
